passages.text: Once again, Jesus spoke to them in parables: “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the chief priests and Pharisees again.
He used parables to teach them.
Jesus said, "The kingdom of heaven is like a king.
This king prepared a wedding banquet for his son."
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν εἶπεν ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λέγων Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ ὅστις ἐποίησεν γάμους τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: He sent his servants to call those he had invited to the banquet, but they refused to come.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people in a parable.
He described the kingdom of heaven.
He said the kingdom is like a king.
The king prepared a wedding banquet for his son.
The king sent his servants.
He told his servants to call those he had invited to the banquet.
The invited people refused to come.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ καλέσαι τοὺς κεκλημένους εἰς τοὺς γάμους καὶ οὐκ ἤθελον ἐλθεῖν

passages.text: Again, he sent other servants and said, ‘Tell those who have been invited that I have prepared my dinner. My oxen and fattened cattle have been killed, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding banquet.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke in a parable about the kingdom of heaven.
The kingdom of heaven is like a king.
The king prepared a wedding banquet for his son.
The king sent other servants again.
He gave them a message for the invited guests.
He said, “Tell the invited guests this:
I have prepared my dinner.
I have killed my oxen and fattened cattle.
Everything is ready.
Come to the wedding banquet.”
passages.original: Πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν ἄλλους δούλους λέγων Εἴπατε τοῖς κεκλημένοις Ἰδοὺ τὸ ἄριστόν μου ἡτοίμακα οἱ ταῦροί μου καὶ τὰ σιτιστὰ τεθυμένα καὶ πάντα ἕτοιμα δεῦτε εἰς τοὺς γάμους

passages.text: But they paid no attention and went away, one to his field, another to his business.
passages.sermon:
The invited guests did not care about the invitation.
They ignored the message.
One man went to his own field.
Another man went to his business.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀμελήσαντες ἀπῆλθον ὃς μὲν εἰς τὸν ἴδιον ἀγρόν ὃς δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν ἐμπορίαν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.
passages.sermon:
Some people did not ignore the king’s invitation.
These people were different from those who went away.
These people seized the king’s servants.
They mistreated the king’s servants.
They killed the king’s servants.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ κρατήσαντες τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ὕβρισαν καὶ ἀπέκτειναν

passages.text: The king was enraged, and he sent his troops to destroy those murderers and burn their city.
passages.sermon:
The king became very angry.
He sent his soldiers.
The soldiers destroyed those murderers.
The soldiers burned their city.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς ὠργίσθη καὶ πέμψας τὰ στρατεύματα αὐτοῦ ἀπώλεσεν τοὺς φονεῖς ἐκείνους καὶ τὴν πόλιν αὐτῶν ἐνέπρησεν

passages.text: Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding banquet is ready, but those I invited were not worthy.
passages.sermon: The king spoke to his servants.\r\nHe said the wedding banquet is ready.\r\nHe said the people he invited were not worthy.
passages.original: τότε λέγει τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ Ὁ μὲν γάμος ἕτοιμός ἐστιν οἱ δὲ κεκλημένοι οὐκ ἦσαν ἄξιοι

passages.text: Go therefore to the crossroads and invite to the banquet as many as you can find.’
passages.sermon: The king spoke to his servants.\r\nHe told them to go out to the crossroads.\r\nHe told them to invite everyone they could find to the wedding banquet.
passages.original: πορεύεσθε οὖν ἐπὶ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὁδῶν καὶ ὅσους ἐὰν εὕρητε καλέσατε εἰς τοὺς γάμους

passages.text: So the servants went out into the streets and gathered everyone they could find, both evil and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.
passages.sermon:
The king had servants.
The king sent his servants into the streets.
The servants went out as the king commanded.
The servants searched for people in the streets.
The servants gathered everyone they found.
They gathered both evil people and good people.
The servants brought all these people together.
The wedding hall became full of guests.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς συνήγαγον πάντας οὓς εὗρον πονηρούς τε καὶ ἀγαθούς καὶ ἐπλήσθη ὁ γάμος ἀνακειμένων

passages.text: But when the king came in to see the guests, he spotted a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes.
passages.sermon:
The king entered the hall.
He wanted to see the guests.
He saw a man there.
This man was not wearing wedding clothes.
passages.original: Εἰσελθὼν δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς θεάσασθαι τοὺς ἀνακειμένους εἶδεν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἐνδεδυμένον ἔνδυμα γάμου

passages.text: ‘Friend,’ he asked, ‘how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’ But the man was speechless.
passages.sermon:
The king saw a man at the wedding feast.
The man did not wear wedding clothes.
The king spoke to the man.
The king said, “Friend, how did you come in here without wedding clothes?”
The man did not answer.
The man was silent.
passages.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ἑταῖρε πῶς εἰσῆλθες ὧδε μὴ ἔχων ἔνδυμα γάμου Ὁ δὲ ἐφιμώθη

passages.text: Then the king told the servants, ‘Tie him hand and foot, and throw him into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
passages.sermon:
The king saw a man at the wedding feast.
This man did not wear wedding clothes.
The king spoke to his servants.
He said, “Tie his hands and feet.”
He said, “Throw him outside into the outer darkness.”
In that place, people will weep.
In that place, people will grind their teeth.
passages.original: Τότε ὁ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν τοῖς διακόνοις Δήσαντες αὐτοῦ πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ἐκβάλετε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων

passages.text: For many are called, but few are chosen.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He explained a truth about God's kingdom.
God calls many people.
He invites them to come.
But only a few people are chosen by God.
Not everyone who is called is chosen.
passages.original: Πολλοὶ γάρ εἰσιν κλητοὶ ὀλίγοι δὲ ἐκλεκτοί

passages.text: Then the Pharisees went out and conspired to trap Jesus in His words.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees were religious leaders.
They left the place where Jesus was.
They made a plan together.
They wanted to trap Jesus.
They tried to catch Him by His own words.
passages.original: Τότε πορευθέντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον ὅπως αὐτὸν παγιδεύσωσιν ἐν λόγῳ

passages.text: They sent their disciples to Him along with the Herodians. “Teacher,” they said, “we know that You are honest and that You teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. You seek favor from no one, because You pay no attention to external appearance.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees sent their disciples to Jesus.
They also sent the Herodians with them.
They spoke to Jesus.
They called Him “Teacher.”
They said, “We know You are honest.”
They said, “You teach the way of God.”
They said, “You teach in truth.”
They said, “You do not seek favor from anyone.”
They said, “You do not pay attention to a person’s outward appearance.”
passages.original: καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτῶν μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ διδάσκεις καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: So tell us what You think: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees and the Herodians spoke to Jesus.
They wanted to trap Jesus with a question.
They said, “Tell us what you think.”
They asked, “Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar?”
They also asked, “Or is it not lawful?”
passages.original: εἰπὸν οὖν ἡμῖν τί σοι δοκεῖ ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ

passages.text: But Jesus knew their evil intent and said, “You hypocrites, why are you testing Me?
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw their evil intent.
Jesus understood what they wanted to do.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “You hypocrites, why are you testing Me?”
passages.original: Γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πονηρίαν αὐτῶν εἶπεν Τί με πειράζετε ὑποκριταί

passages.text: Show Me the coin used for the tax.” And they brought Him a denarius.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people who questioned Him.\r\nHe said, “Show Me the coin used for the tax.”\r\nThe people brought Jesus a denarius.
passages.original: ἐπιδείξατέ μοι τὸ νόμισμα τοῦ κήνσου Οἱ δὲ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ δηνάριον

passages.text: “Whose image is this,” He asked, “and whose inscription?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
He showed them a coin.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Whose image is this?”
He also said, “Whose inscription is this?”
passages.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή

passages.text: “Caesar’s,” they answered. So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”
passages.sermon:
The people answered Jesus.
They said, “Caesar’s.”
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “Give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar.”
Jesus also said, “Give to God what belongs to God.”
passages.original: Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Καίσαρος Τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἀπόδοτε οὖν τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: And when they heard this, they were amazed. So they left Him and went away.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He answered their question about paying taxes to Caesar.
The people listened to Jesus.
They heard His answer.
They were amazed at His wisdom.
They left Jesus.
They went away from Him.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες ἐθαύμασαν καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθαν

passages.text: That same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him.
passages.sermon: The Sadducees came to Jesus that same day.\r\nThe Sadducees say there is no resurrection.\r\nThey questioned Jesus.
passages.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ Σαδδουκαῖοι λέγοντες μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν

passages.text: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses declared that if a man dies without having children, his brother is to marry the widow and raise up offspring for him.
passages.sermon:
The Sadducees spoke to Jesus.
They called Him Teacher.
They said, “Moses gave us a command.”
Moses said, “If a man dies and has no children, his brother must marry the dead man’s wife.”
The brother must have children with her.
These children will carry on the dead brother’s name.
passages.original: λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν Ἐάν τις ἀποθάνῃ μὴ ἔχων τέκνα ἐπιγαμβρεύσει ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναστήσει σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Now there were seven brothers among us. The first one married and died without having children. So he left his wife to his brother.
passages.sermon:
There were seven brothers among us.
The first brother married a wife.
He died.
He had no children.
He left his wife to his brother.
passages.original: ἦσαν δὲ παρ’ ἡμῖν ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοί καὶ ὁ πρῶτος γήμας ἐτελεύτησεν καὶ μὴ ἔχων σπέρμα ἀφῆκεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: The same thing happened to the second and third brothers, down to the seventh.
passages.sermon:
The second brother married the widow.
He died without children.
He left the woman to his brother.
The third brother did the same.
Each brother, up to the seventh, married her in turn.
Each brother died without children.
Each brother left the woman to the next brother.
passages.original: ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ δεύτερος καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἕως τῶν ἑπτά

passages.text: And last of all, the woman died.
passages.sermon:
There were seven brothers.
Each brother married the same woman, one after another.
Each brother died.
The woman outlived all seven brothers.
After all the brothers died, the woman also died.
passages.original: ὕστερον δὲ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ἡ γυνή

passages.text: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be of the seven? For all of them were married to her.”
passages.sermon:
Seven brothers each married the same woman.
All seven brothers had her as a wife.
Later, the woman also died.
People asked about the resurrection.
They asked, "In the resurrection, whose wife will she be of the seven?"
All seven brothers had been married to her.
passages.original: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει οὖν τίνος τῶν ἑπτὰ ἔσται γυνή πάντες γὰρ ἔσχον αὐτήν

passages.text: Jesus answered, “You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus answered their question.
Jesus said, “You are mistaken.
You do not know the Scriptures.
You do not know the power of God.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: In the resurrection, people will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.
passages.sermon: In the resurrection, people will not marry.\r\nPeople will not be given in marriage.\r\nPeople will be like the angels in heaven.
passages.original: ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀναστάσει οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται ἀλλ’ ὡς ἄγγελοι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ εἰσιν

passages.text: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what God said to you: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to people who questioned the resurrection of the dead.
Jesus referred to the words of God in the Scriptures.
God said, “I am the God of Abraham.”
God said, “I am the God of Isaac.”
God said, “I am the God of Jacob.”
God is not the God of the dead.
God is the God of the living.
passages.original: περὶ δὲ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῶν νεκρῶν οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑμῖν ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ λέγοντος Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ Θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ Θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ Θεὸς Ἰακώβ οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ Θεὸς νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων

passages.text: When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at His teaching.
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught the people.
The crowds listened to Him.
The crowds heard His words.
The crowds felt great astonishment at His teaching.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And when the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they themselves gathered together.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees were a group of Jewish religious leaders.
Jesus had just silenced the Sadducees.
The Pharisees heard about this.
The Pharisees gathered together.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἐφίμωσεν τοὺς Σαδδουκαίους συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό

passages.text: One of them, an expert in the law, tested Him with a question: “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?”
passages.sermon:
A group of Pharisees gathered together.
One man in the group was an expert in the law.
This expert wanted to test Jesus.
He asked Jesus a question.
He said, “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?”
passages.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν νομικὸς πειράζων αὐτόν Διδάσκαλε ποία ἐντολὴ μεγάλη ἐν τῷ νόμῳ

passages.text: Jesus declared, “ ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the expert in the law.
Jesus said, "Love the Lord your God."
Love Him with all your heart.
Love Him with all your soul.
Love Him with all your mind.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου

passages.text: This is the first and greatest commandment.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke about the commandments.\r\nHe said, "This is the first commandment."\r\nThis commandment is the greatest commandment.
passages.original: αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μεγάλη καὶ πρώτη ἐντολή

passages.text: And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He gave them a command.
This command is the second greatest commandment.
It is like the first commandment.
Jesus said, “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
passages.original: δευτέρα δὲ ὁμοία αὐτῇ Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν

passages.text: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”
passages.sermon:
God gave commandments to His people.
God gave many laws through Moses.
God spoke through the prophets.
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said there are two great commandments.
All the Law depends on these two commandments.
All the teachings of the prophets depend on these two commandments.
passages.original: ἐν ταύταις ταῖς δυσὶν ἐντολαῖς ὅλος ὁ νόμος κρέμαται καὶ οἱ προφῆται

passages.text: While the Pharisees were assembled, Jesus questioned them: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?” “David’s,” they answered.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees gathered together.
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
Jesus asked them a question.
Jesus said, “What do you think about the Christ?”
Jesus said, “Whose son is the Christ?”
The Pharisees answered Jesus.
They said, “The Christ is David’s son.”
passages.original: Συνηγμένων δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ περὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ τίνος υἱός ἐστιν Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Τοῦ Δαυίδ

passages.text: Jesus said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call Him ‘Lord’? For he says: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.” ’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
Jesus asked them a question.
He said, “David was guided by the Holy Spirit.”
David called the Christ ‘Lord.’
David said, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand.”’
‘Remain there until I put your enemies under your feet.’
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτοῖς Πῶς οὖν Δαυὶδ ἐν Πνεύματι καλεῖ αὐτὸν Κύριον λέγων Εἶπεν Κύριος τῷ Κυρίῳ μου Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου Ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου Ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου

passages.text: So if David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how can He be David’s son?”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David called the Christ “Lord.”
David spoke by the Holy Spirit.
David showed respect and authority to the Christ.
David called the Christ greater than himself.
The Christ is called David’s son.
A son is usually less important than his father.
If David calls the Christ “Lord,” the Christ must be greater than David.
How can the Christ be both David’s son and David’s Lord?
passages.original: Εἰ οὖν Δαυὶδ καλεῖ αὐτὸν Κύριον πῶς υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἐστιν

passages.text: No one was able to answer a word, and from that day on no one dared to question Him any further.
passages.sermon: No one could answer Jesus.\r\nNo one spoke a word in reply to Him.\r\nFrom that day on, no one dared to ask Jesus any more questions.
passages.original: Καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο ἀποκριθῆναι αὐτῷ λόγον οὐδὲ ἐτόλμησέν τις ἀπ’ ἐκείνης τῆς ἡμέρας ἐπερωτῆσαι αὐτὸν οὐκέτι
